issue_snapshot.title: Group page with sections, expenses list and settings entry
issue_snapshot.body:
A group member finds the balance, the expenses, and the next action without scrolling one long stack, with Add expense always one tap away.

UI face: group member sees one organised page (summary plus tabbed Expenses, Balances and settle up, Activity, Members) with Add expense always reachable and settings tucked behind Settings. Contract face: consumes shell, tokens, rows, cards, segmented control, dialogs, and skeletons from piece 1; reuses existing group, expense-list, balance, and activity-excerpt reads with no endpoint or schema change. Follows docs/ui.md Group page structure and states exactly.

**Out of scope**
- Expense editor form internals and settle-up sheet internals (next piece)
- Balance-math, simplification, filter semantics, or activity-writing changes
- Dark mode

Covers: TR-11, S-8
Part of #31.
Depends on #33.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Group page shows shell with back-to-Home breadcrumb, group header (mark, name, currency badge, Settings entry), and a summary card with the user balance as hero number, who-owes-whom lines, primary Add expense and secondary Settle up.
- **IAC-2** Sections render as tabs or segmented control: Expenses, Balances and settle up, Activity excerpt linking to the full feed, Members excerpt linking to members; settings (rename, archive) live behind the Settings entry, never on the main scroll.
- **IAC-3** Expenses section shows newest-first rows (avatar left, title plus human-date metadata middle, amount right with words-plus-colour) with search plus member and category filters inside a disclosure on phones.
- **IAC-4** Row actions live in an overflow menu (edit, delete with confirm naming the expense); no inline Edit or red Delete buttons on rows; destructive choices confirm in a dialog or sheet.
- **IAC-5** Add expense is always reachable: header button on desktop and fixed bottom button on phones; empty group shows what-to-do-first with an Add-expense button and a settled banner when all balances are zero.
- **IAC-6** Loading shows skeleton summary card, section tabs, and three expense rows with no layout shift; a failed section shows inline retry inside its own panel; full failure shows a page error with retry, never a half-rendered ledger.
- **IAC-7** Dates read as people say them and times render in the viewer zone; works at 375px and 1280px (desktop may place summary in a side card); keyboard, focus, headings, and reduced-motion rules from ui.md hold.

review.title: A repeated ?section= query key crashes the group page instead of defaulting to expenses.
review.detail:
A repeated ?section= query key crashes the group page instead of defaulting to expenses.

`lib/groups/validation.ts:165`

Evidence: lib/groups/validation.ts:165 does (raw ?? '').trim().toLowerCase(). Next.js delivers searchParams values as string | string[], so ?section=expenses&section=balances hands groupSectionFrom a string[], on which .trim() throws TypeError. GroupPage parses section at app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:119 before the ledger try/catch, so the throw escapes to the route error boundary rather than rendering the expenses panel that AC-2/AC-10 require for malformed input.

Fix: Coerce before trimming, e.g. const value = (Array.isArray(raw) ? raw[0] : raw ?? '').trim().toLowerCase(). Note activityFilterFrom and expenseFiltersFrom share the pattern; fixing only the new parser leaves the same crash on ?activity= and ?q=.

`app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:75`

Evidence: app/groups/[id]/page.tsx:75: 'the panels are server-rendered, and a reader without JavaScript gets all four.' Under App Router streaming with the route-level loading.tsx boundary, the resolved ledger waits in the hidden Flight payload for the client-JS swap, so a scriptless reader keeps the skeleton plus the <noscript> notice (loading.tsx) — not the four panels. review.title: The old UTC-label timestamp implementation in ui-interactive.tsx is stranded: this PR migrates its only product consumer (activity-feed) to components/timestamp.tsx, leaving two time-rendering systems and a `Timestamp` export that reintroduces the banned UTC label if a later ticket reaches for it.
review.detail:
The old UTC-label timestamp implementation in ui-interactive.tsx is stranded: this PR migrates its only product consumer (activity-feed) to components/timestamp.tsx, leaving two time-rendering systems and a `Timestamp` export that reintroduces the banned UTC label if a later ticket reaches for it.

`components/ui-interactive.tsx:232`

The stranded cluster (ui-interactive.tsx:142-244) is product-dead.

review.title: On a failed /activity read, the filter chips drop the ?group= scope even when it is known, and the retry drops it whenever the groups read itself failed.
review.detail:
On a failed /activity read, the filter chips drop the ?group= scope even when it is known, and the retry drops it whenever the groups read itself failed.

`app/activity/page.tsx:127`

Evidence: app/activity/page.tsx:127 renders <FilterChips filter={filter} action="/activity" /> with no preserved prop in the failed branch, while the success branch (:154) passes preserved={...ACTIVITY_GROUP_PARAM...}. So any failed scoped load loses the scope the moment the reader touches a chip. The retry at :140 uses scoped?.id, but scoped (:80) is resolved from groups, which stays [] when listActivityGroups throws — so a groups-read failure also strips ?group= from the retry URL.

Fix: Pass the same preserved map in the failed branch (lift scoped-or-raw-group computation above the failed/success split), and build the retry href from the raw query group param as fallback when groups failed to load, e.g. activityHref(filter, scoped?.id ?? query[ACTIVITY_GROUP_PARAM] ?? null).

Observed identically on the PR-untouched /members page ("Loading members…").

repro: Create any group with an expense as a signed-in user.
Open a fresh browser context with JavaScript disabled and the session cookies.
Goto /groups/<id>?section=expenses and read document.body: the visible root holds only the loading fallback while body > div[hidden] > div holds the full page.
Repeat on /groups/<id>/members (code untouched by this PR): identical skeleton-only result.
